articles.excerpt: After having this spot saved on Google Maps for quite some time, I took my bike and cycled all the way to Biesenthal and it was worthwhile indeed.

blocks.content:
I got a little special interest in artsy, dreamy and whimsical museums. The closer they are to nature and interesting landscapes, the better. I stumbled across Wehmühle some years ago, put it on my Google Maps "to visit" list and never got there. This year, there was a substantial itch and I finally needed to go there, as my Instagram algorithm pushed this place on me multiple times. As I do not have a car, I had to go there by bicycle. This worked out kinda fine and after surviving the Berlin traffic and finding my way through a grey-ist north-eastern Berlin, I cycled along fields, lakes, the Autobahn and finally found Wehrmuehle at the end of a forest path.

It grew on me very quickly. Loved the curation of the different artworks and especially the transcendence from the art space to the local nature reserve. It felt really remote and far away from the usual Berlin noise. After a Campari Spritz and a piece of apple pie, I returned and I definitely need to come back sooner than later.

articles.title: a visit to wehrmuehle

articles.excerpt: I pushed myself to do some photowalks after regular 9-5 duty and between weekend relaxation and came across some interesting perspectives and berlin summer vibes.

blocks.content:
As this is the first article, I am sharing on this little blog, a short introduction may be worthwhile. In addition to the usual instagram spam, I would like to set up a little outlet for sharing my photography and related thoughts. There will be a strong Berlin focus, but other locations and places will follow. 

To have an easy start, I would like to share a quick recap of august 2026 photowalks, which led me to summery Kreuzberg, Hansaviertel and Mitte.

slides.caption: stopping by the notorious voo store
and having some spectacular lighting at Kotti

blocks.content: I know Berlin is multifaceted and there is not one specific Berlin, but a summery evening in Kreuzberg is one of the most Berlin things. Hanging out next to Landwehrkanal, strolling along Reichenberger Str. or having a drink at the usual suspects like Ankerklause - there is a certain magic.

slides.caption: scenery with some Oscar Niemeyer in the background

blocks.content:
I stumbled upon Hansaviertel two years ago on Instagram after overseeing this place for quite some time. And now I am kinda obsessed with the architecture and I found myself a new favorite café at the heart of it. Is this location spectacular or mind boggling - certainly not, but I like the modernism and I am into the idea, that this was built with a certain vision in mind.

To conclude the recap I got some snapshots of Mitte Mitte. Is this area a bit snobby and performative - yes. But it is still a cute little microcosm and always offers some nice motives and perspectives.

articles.title: august photo recap

articles.excerpt: I took the U3 to southwest Berlin. In close proximity to Grunewald and Krumme Lanke, there is a museum which hits all the spots - excellent curation, nice interior, whimsical outdoor area and a very good café.

blocks.content:
My relationship to southwest Berlin is a bit ambiguous. On the one hand, I was very glad moving out of this part of the city after living there for nearly four years. The long bus and S-Bahn rides were a pain in the ass and I never felt truly at home. In addition, it is a part of West-Berlin which does not really resonate with me. Steglitz looks a bit like an average West-German town and like Charlottenburg it seems to be a completely different world. In a way it is very much Berlin but at the same time it is not (at least from my point of view). But on the other hand, it is indeed very special how Berlin slowly transcends from metropolis to forests, lakes and nature in general.

An of course there are some (hidden) gems like the Liebermann Villa on the shores of Wannsee, there is the Brücke Museum, the Mexikoplatz, Krumme Lanke and Schlachtensee, Pfaueninsel and Haus am Waldsee. The latter is one of my favorite museums in Berlin due to the extraordinary combination of curation, interior, exterior and café. It ticks all the boxes. I came across this place 3 years ago in the context of 2023 Berlin Art Week and was immediately enchanted. Even though it is quite popular, the atmosphere remains very intimate and in my view this strengthens the experience of the displayed artworks. I am also a big fan of its niche and bespoke curations. 10/10 will always recommend ;-)

slides.caption: full view of the historic building

articles.title: southwest berlin whimsy

articles.excerpt: The search for some interesting scenes and something new besides my usual Kreuzberg or Neukölln photowalks led me to the infamous Wedding.

blocks.content: Well, the Wedding… For the last twenty years people kept saying „der Wedding kommt“ referring to pre-gentrification state of this Bezirk and the long wait for another Prenzlauer Berg-ification or Neukölln-ification. I am not sure whether the Wedding should come and I really doubt whether the locals would benefit from it. Maybe the truth lies in the middle and the mix of working-class neighborhoods, migrant culture, old west-berlin charm next to the new-age listening bars and fine dining spaces is the way to go. I am not a sociologist or an expert concerning urbanism but I am in favor of diverse and mixed-up neighborhoods instead of monocultural areas. But to be honest, the gentrification and the price hikes have already hit this area and will continue to change the face of this part of Berlin.

slides.caption: a curry wurst staple at Gesundbrunnen - strong recommendation

blocks.content:
With this in mind I started my walk at Gesundbrunnen with a quick pit stop at Curry Baude, strolled north to Pankstraße and to Osloer Straße. Even though it reminded me of Neukölln, there is a completely different vibe and this is what I love about Berlin. I cannot really phrase it or narrow it down but it felt distinct and different.

After crossing the small river Panke and crossed the Leopoldplatz. I stumbled upon fine dining restaurants, specialty coffee shops and creative agencies. So, there we are - in-between two worlds or in-between two different stages of Berlin development.

articles.title: der wedding kommt

articles.excerpt: September is Berlin Art Week time and especially Positions Art Fair is the place to be, when it comes to indulging in various art and to do some people watching.

blocks.content: I am not an artist and I am not very connected to the art scene in general, but I really enjoy visiting a well-curated gallery or an architecturally sophisticated museum. Absorbing artworks and being in aesthetically pleasing spaces is a quite important source of inspiration for me. Therefore and due to the fact that I am haunted by social anxiety, Berlin Art Week comes in handy because of the easy access to snobby galleries and the special formats, like guided tours etc.. Especially the latter proved to be worthwhile and insightful. Additionally it is very important to avoid over-pacing and putting too many spots on the agenda. Do not underestimate the size of Berlin when it comes to having a "quick“ walk from one place to another.

This year I ended up at Positions Art Fair in the old Tempelhof airport, which is always a highlight because of the high density of works and more or less "artsy“ people. It is a place to absorb the atmosphere and to mingle with the crowd. This year there were only a few positions, that resonated with me.

Second point an my agenda was a tour along Leipziger Strasse which is not only a larger than life reminiscence of the good old socialist days but also housing some little galleries.

To finish my art week visit, I ended up in Mitte on Augustrasse - where else. As described in another article, the Bermuda triangle of Auguststrasse and Linienstrasse is also stacked with galleries and seems like a little parallel universe in the heart of Berlin. 

And after not buying any pricy paintings or sculptures, there is still the chance to grab an aesthetic publication at Do you read me, to carry something home.

articles.title: art week maxxing

articles.excerpt: There is a short period in-between late summer and early fall, when Berlin turns golden and leads you to believe, that summer is not over and winter will not be as cruel as last year.

blocks.content: Fall is my favorite time of the year. As my birthday is in October, I feel deeply connected to this season and I really enjoy the beginning of the transition process, which will ultimately lead to a cold Berlin winter. The latter has to be put aside for now, as I want to focus on the more warm and more pleasant part of fall. Crunchy leaves and fall foliage are quite magical, and you can really sense a certain crispness in the air as it gets a bit chilly as well as windy. It’s time to dress up in a cozy way and enjoy the last bits of summer, before Berlin turns the lever and it gets grey and gloomy.

My first photowalk led me to the god old farmers market at Boxi, which is a household name and always worthwhile. It has become quite a rendezvous point for granola moms from Friedrichshain and the usual Berlin hipsters, who have gentrified this part of Berlin, which was once a blue-collar neighborhood. Nevertheless, as I don’t want to sound rude, it is a nice mix of people, I recommend getting some sourdough bread from KEIT and restocking fresh produce from local farmers.

slides.caption: at the usual Kreuzkölln hangout spots

blocks.content: For the second photowalk, I chose one of my favorite routes from Schlesisches Tor to Körnerpark, which is indeed a long haul, but there are so many nice spaces, places and details along the way.

articles.title: golden october
